summary.text: A 47-year-old female with a history of alcohol-induced chronic pancreatitis and alcohol use disorder presented in June 2024 with hematochezia, melena and syncope. On admission she showed low blood pressure and tachycardia, with hemoglobin 7.1 g/dL and serum lipase 449 U/L. Urgent CT angiography, chosen over initial endoscopy to rule out vascular complications, revealed a splenic artery pseudoaneurysm at the junction of the pancreatic body and tail next to a pancreatic head pseudocyst.

She had immediate visceral angiography with successful coil embolization of the pseudoaneurysm, and angiography confirmed total occlusion; covered stent placement was considered but not pursued because of vessel tortuosity and caliber. She was discharged with alcohol cessation counseling and plans for outpatient follow-up. Referral to addiction medicine and psychiatric services was made but engagement was limited, and the pseudocyst was observed without intervention.

Over the next three months she had recurrent admissions for alcohol-induced pancreatitis (peak lipase 527 U/L), continued drinking heavily and developed alcoholic hepatitis, pulmonary embolism and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction. Serial CT imaging up to 3 months after embolization showed a fluctuating pseudocyst and, on the last scan, no evidence of significant aneurysm recanalization. Long-term surveillance then lapsed because of patient non-compliance.

Eight months after the initial embolization she was found unresponsive in pulseless electrical activity arrest and, after return of spontaneous circulation, remained critically hypotensive with lactate 19.7 mmol/L and hemoglobin 6.4 g/dL. Emergency laparotomy revealed massive hemoperitoneum from rupture of the previously embolized pseudoaneurysm; the splenic artery was ligated and over 55 units of blood products were given. Refractory shock, anuric acute kidney injury, DIC and multi-organ failure followed, care was transitioned to comfort measures and she died.
